name: What is the best layout for a small primary bath expansion?

mainEntity.name: What layout gives the most space and function in a small primary bathroom expansion?
mainEntity.text: What layout gives the most space and function in a small primary bathroom expansion?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a small primary bath expansion, the best layout usually focuses on open circulation and fixture efficiency rather than trying to fit every luxury item. A larger walk-in shower often creates more usable space than a tub-shower combo. A single vanity with better storage can work better than forcing in a double vanity that crowds the room. Pocket doors, frameless glass, recessed medicine cabinets, and wall-mounted vanities all help the bathroom feel larger. In compact Los Angeles homes, the design should also account for the doorway swing, towel storage, and where wet traffic will land after shower use. If the expansion is modest, the main goal is to remove bottlenecks and improve sightlines. The bathroom will feel bigger when the most visible surfaces are clean and continuous, not chopped up by awkward partitions. A good layout review should be done before demolition so the expanded space actually improves daily use rather than just increasing dimensions on paper.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best small primary bath layout usually prioritizes a larger shower, a single well-placed vanity, clear circulation space, and storage built into the walls. Pocket doors, glass shower panels, and wall-mounted fixtures can make the room feel bigger without adding much square footage.
